name: Question 4
problem: Use the method of Lagrange multipliers to find the minimum value of the function $f(x,y)=2{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+1\,$ on the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4.$
worked_solution:
We must find the minimum value of $f(x,y)$ subject to the constraint $g(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4.$ 

Since $f(x,y)$ is continuous and the constraint is closed and bounded, $f(x,y)$ reaches a global maximum and a global minimum on the constraint. 

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
∇f(x,y)=\lambda ∇g(x,y),\,g(x,y)=4
$$

We start by solving the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y) \\ ⟨{f}_{x}(x,y),{f}_{y}(x,y)⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x}(x,y),{g}_{y}(x,y)⟩ \\ ⟨4x,-2y⟩ & =\lambda ⟨2x,2y⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}4x=2\lambda x \\ -2y=2\lambda y\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}x(2-\lambda )=0 \\ y(\lambda +1)=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this system, we break it up into several cases:

- Assuming $x=0$ in the first equation of the system, the constraint condition ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4=0$ implies

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-4 & =0\,⇒\,y=\pm 2.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the critical points $(0,-2),(0,2).$

- Assuming $\lambda =2$ in the first equation of the system, the second equation of the system implies

$$
\begin{aligned}y(2+1)=0\,⇒\,y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the constraint condition ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-4=0$ implies

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\pm 2.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the critical points $(2,0),(-2,0).$

Therefore, $f$ has possible extreme values at the points

$$
(0,\pm 2),\,(\pm 2,0).
$$

We evaluate $f$ at these points. These are given in the following table:

| $(x,y)$ | $(0,\pm 2)$ | $(\pm 2,0)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x,y)$ | $-3$ | $9$ |

Therefore, the function reaches a minimum value at the points $(0,\pm 2)$ and its minimum value is $-3.$
